arrays:
📦 Array is a collection of elements stored in contiguous memory. 
🔹 All elements are of the same data type. 
🔹 Each element can be accessed using an index (starting from 0). 
🔹 Arrays allow fast access (O(1)) but insertion/deletion can be costly. 
🚀 Common operations include traversal, insertion, deletion, and searching.
strings:
🔤 String is a sequence of characters. 
🔹 Strings can be immutable (like in Python) or mutable depending on the language. 
🔹 Each character has an index. 
🔹 Common operations include concatenation, slicing, searching, and comparison. 
✨ Strings are widely used in text processing and pattern matching.
stack:
📚 Stack is a linear data structure that follows the LIFO (Last In, First Out) principle. 
🔹 The last element inserted is the first one to be removed. 
🔹 Basic operations include push (insert), pop (remove), and peek/top (view top element). 
🔹 All operations are typically O(1). 
🔹 Stacks can be implemented using arrays or linked lists. 
🚀 Common applications include expression evaluation, recursion (call stack), undo/redo operations, and syntax parsing.
queue:
🚏 Queue is a linear data structure that follows the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle. 
🔹 The first element inserted is the first one to be removed. 
🔹 Basic operations include enqueue (insert), dequeue (remove), front (view first element), and rear (view last element). 
🔹 Insertion happens at the rear and deletion happens at the front. 
🔹 All basic operations are typically O(1). 
🚀 Common applications include CPU scheduling, printer queues, buffering, BFS traversal, and request handling systems.
